transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

Well, thank you for seeing me. It's... it's about bridges. What brings me in is that the moment a bridge crossing becomes unavoidable, I get this terrible rush of fear. It happens before I’m even on the bridge itself. My heart just starts pounding, and my hands go completely damp on the steering wheel—or the armrest, if someone else is driving. It's just a very intense, immediate reaction.
Is this fear limited to certain types of bridges, such as high bridges, long bridges, or bridges over water, or does it happen with all bridges regardless of their structure or location?

It's mainly the high ones. I mean, I know perfectly well that thousands of cars cross those bridges every single day without any trouble at all. But... when I see a high span on the map, or if I catch sight of it up ahead through the windshield, it just feels to me as if the whole thing is waiting to drop away right out from under us.
